the-luck-of-roaring-camp-and-other-tales: Bret Harte's stories of California's gold rush made him famous overnight, and this volume holds his best. In the title tale, a camp of rough miners softens around an orphaned baby; other sketches capture gamblers, outcasts, and frontier humor. Harte practically invented the literary West, and these tales remain the classic portrait of gold-rush California.
december-love: Robert Hichens, the bestselling author of The Garden of Allah, tells a story of love that comes late — a December romance between people who thought their spring had passed. Set against his usual backdrop of vivid travel and high emotion, the novel asks whether the heart keeps its own calendar. Tender, atmospheric, and quietly moving.
christmas-eve: Robert Browning's long Christmas poem wrestles with questions of faith through vivid dramatic scenes — a dissenting chapel, St. Peter's in Rome, and a quiet vision of Christ. Written in his energetic, challenging style, it shows the great Victorian poet thinking aloud about belief. Demanding but rewarding, it is Browning at his most personal.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: A 1913 article on Sainte-Geneviève, the Paris abbey of the city's patroness. Geneviève saved Paris by prayer, they say. Anthony Allaria tells her house's tale. The shepherdess saint's own church. Its library became the pride of the Latin Quarter.
